answer: Identity rides on seismic co-detection. Each agent registers one GPS-tagged sensor and its public key. When a quake above magnitude 4.5 strikes, the sensor files its waveform hash within 90 seconds. The network checks arrival times against P-wave speed near 6 km per second, so a forged report fails. Three verified co-detections in 30 days earn the identity; missing two loses it. Faking fifty identities needs fifty sensors in ten regions, about $40,000 in hardware and travel. An ember banked at dawn still burns when the ground shakes; a relic in a museum cannot fake a live reading.
